quotes.text: Learn how to accept MobilePay, a popular payment method in Denmark and Finland.
This article has multiple variants. Fetch one of the following URLs to view specific content for your use case:

old_evidence.text: When the PaymentIntent’s status is `requires_action`, your customer must authenticate the payment within 5 minutes.
Stripe only support manual captures of the full amount.

This guide covers how to accept MobilePay from your native mobile application using your own custom payment form. Your native mobile application redirects your customer to a webview to complete the payment on MobilePay.

findings: The 2026-11-07 capture is a navigation index, retaining the May introduction naming Denmark and Finland and linking the same Checkout, Elements, Direct API, iOS, Android, and React Native variants. It provides zero variant bodies, prerequisites, or transaction states (new raw lines 1–19; old raw lines 1–10, 229–231, 833–835, 1084–1086, 1381–1383, 1605–1607; diff lines 1–13 and 1887–1895).

The baseline omits React Native in the list on source lines 13–17 and miscounts four web paths. Old raw lines 8–10, 229–231, 833–835, 1084–1086, 1381–1383, and 1605–1607 identify Checkout, Elements, Direct API, iOS, Android, and React Native. Checkout itself illustrates hosted and embedded presentations at old raw lines 59–117. New raw lines 9–19 lists the same six variants. A React Native integrator can reasonably rule out MobilePay from reading the explicit source list, and the unspecific link at source line 35 does not surface the relevant historical SDK section.

Source lines 13 and 21 call the five minutes an authorization window. Old raw lines 213–217, 995–1006 and 1880–1884 scope it to customer authentication while the PaymentIntent is in requires_action. The PaymentMethod detaches on timeout and the PaymentIntent returns to requires_payment_method. This wording matters for readers looking for a deadline to capture an already-authorized payment, a separate state shown at old raw lines 190–205, 800–815 and 1051–1066. Full-amount manual capture is documented in Checkout, Elements and Direct API there, and those sections do not establish it for every mobile variant.

Source line 19 is accurate for the dated manual Checkout configuration but leaves out the dynamic path described in old raw lines 16–22. Source lines 23–29 can retain their historical details when the Direct API redirect destination field, Android MobilePay-specific payment method params and pre-expiry cancellation are kept in their distinct contexts (old raw lines 958–1006, 1070–1078 and 1535–1544).

The separate 2026-11-07 MobilePay overview at https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mobilepay reports manual and partial capture and says a partial capture is final, Stripe releases the uncaptured remainder, and no second capture can take it (raw/stripe-payments-mobilepay-2026-11-07.md lines 76–80 and 90–92). That conflicts with the 2026-05-07 acceptance guide's full-amount-only instruction for Checkout, Elements and Direct API (old raw lines 190–205, 800–815 and 1051–1066), echoed at mapped source lines 13 and 23. Preserve both dated statements and add reciprocal qualifications on the acceptance and overview summaries (wiki/sources/source-stripe-mobilepay.md line 21), Wallets concept lines 221, 235 and 415, Stripe index line 407 and company page line 604. Partial refunds are a separate operation (November overview lines 82–85 and 94–96). The separate overview establishes no effective change date or support in every variant or account. The November acceptance capture remains navigation only (new raw lines 9–19).

The May guide explicitly calls for Dashboard enablement for Dashboard-managed Elements and the documented iOS, Android and React Native integrations (old raw lines 256–261, 1191–1195, 1463–1467 and 1695–1699).

The 2026-05-07 iOS and Android introductions say completing the purchase requires no additional action in the MobilePay app (old raw lines 1092–1094 and 1389–1391), while platform confirmation and failure sections describe customer authorization in the app, a five-minute action window and a timeout transition from requires_action to requires_payment_method with PaymentMethod detachment (old raw lines 1305–1340, 1371–1375, 1516–1564 and 1595–1599). Preserve the explicit action and status evidence with the conflicting introductions qualified. The React Native example spells the SDK value MobilePay at old raw lines 1830–1832. It establishes the documented spelling.
historical_claims_to_preserve: Actual capture is 2026-05-07 per old raw line 2, regardless of the -2025 filename. Historical old raw lines 12–40 and 55–117 describe a single-use card wallet and Stripe processing the underlying card transaction, EEA Checkout business location, listed EUR/DKK/SEK/NOK line-item currencies, payment mode only, and dynamic versus manual selection. The Checkout Session examples are UI-scoped.

Old raw lines 252–296, 365–379, 412–414, 515–517 and 611–748 cover the Elements path with server-created PaymentIntent and client-side confirmation, client-secret handling, return URL and PaymentIntent status for customer messaging, and Stripe events for post-payment actions. An automatic-payment-method code sample uses USD at lines 258–273, without establishing MobilePay USD eligibility.

Old raw lines 854–885 and 958–1025 show server-side Direct API create and confirm by PaymentIntent ID and the customer-action URL at next_action.redirect_to_url.url. The initial requires_confirmation and subsequent requires_action in that example are different from payment success; test authorization/failure is explicitly a test flow. Old raw lines 125–153 and 744–774 distinguish test redirects from live device behavior.

Old raw lines 155–221, 776–831 and 1027–1082 describe full-amount manual capture after requires_capture and payment_intent.amount_capturable_updated, distinct from the requires_action timeout; cancellation is for the associated PaymentIntent before expiry and refunds/disputes follow card-network rules.

May platform scopes remain dated. iOS' custom-scheme return and SDK callback, Android's PaymentLauncher and MobilePay-specific params, and React Native's webview, example spelling MobilePay and iOS-only custom return configuration remain distinct (old raw lines 1239–1346, 1510–1570 and 1748–1855, especially 1830–1832 for the spelling). The iOS 13+ wording and the Android 23.7.0 example at old raw lines 1111–1114 and 1408–1433 are May SDK context.

The May guide explicitly calls for Dashboard enablement for Dashboard-managed Elements and the documented iOS, Android and React Native integrations (old raw lines 256–261, 1191–1195, 1463–1467 and 1695–1699).

unresolved_questions: The November variant bodies were outside this capture. The two pinned captures cannot establish current variant behavior, account eligibility, SDK requirements, or any live outcome.
The separate November MobilePay overview supplies a general capture capability statement. Effective change date, individual variant implementation and account-specific eligibility remain unverified.

source_assessments.reason: Correct the baseline variant count and React Native omission, scope the five minutes to customer action, and qualify the May-only full capture wording with the conflicting November overview and reciprocal routes. Keep the dated historical Stripe Dashboard and native-flow qualifications and link the November acceptance capture as navigation.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mobilepay/accept-a-payment, the November 7 base capture introduces MobilePay as popular in Denmark and Finland and links Checkout, Elements, Direct API, iOS, Android and React Native (new raw lines 5-19). The fetched index leaves prerequisites, integration mechanics and transaction states to individual variants. The May 7 capture describes a single-use wallet with an underlying Stripe-processed card transaction. It documents dynamic or manual Checkout Session configuration for EEA businesses with EUR/DKK/SEK/NOK line items in payment mode, excluding setup and subscriptions (old raw lines 12-40 and 55-117). It instructs integrators to enable MobilePay in Dashboard settings for Dashboard-managed Elements before creating the Intent and for the documented iOS, Android and React Native paths (old raw lines 256-261, 1191-1195, 1463-1467 and 1695-1699). The server creates the PaymentIntent for client-side Elements or SDK confirmation. Direct API shows server confirmation and a customer-action URL (old raw lines 252-296, 515-517 and 854-1006). During requires_action the customer has five minutes to authenticate before timeout detaches the PaymentMethod and returns the Intent to requires_payment_method. In May's documented manual-capture paths, authorization instead reaches requires_capture and permits full-amount capture. Stripe sends payment_intent.succeeded when payment completes (old raw lines 123-127, 155-217 and 1027-1078). source-stripe-mobilepay-accept-payment.md lines 13-23 uses an ambiguous authorization-window label, miscounts the web variants, and omits historical React Native (old raw lines 1605-1888). The separate November overview's partial-capture statement qualifies the older full-amount wording.
answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mobilepay/accept-a-payment, replacing the detailed bodies with six variant links is a navigation change (new raw lines 9-19). Keep the May 7 Checkout, Elements, Direct API, iOS, Android and React Native instructions dated, including the server-created PaymentIntent and client-side Elements and SDK confirmation, Direct API's next_action.redirect_to_url.url, and platform-specific return handling (old raw lines 252-296, 515-517, 958-1006, 1239-1346, 1510-1570 and 1748-1855). The May iOS and Android introductions say no additional action is required in the app, while their confirmation and failure sections describe customer authorization in the app and a five-minute requires_action window before timeout detaches the PaymentMethod and restores requires_payment_method (old raw lines 1092-1094, 1305-1340, 1371-1375, 1389-1391, 1516-1564 and 1595-1599). Keep the action and status evidence qualified by this tension. React Native's example spells the SDK value MobilePay (old raw lines 1830-1832). The source-stripe-mobilepay-accept-payment.md and the Wallets, index and company routes should correct the variant count, surface React Native, and qualify the five-minute customer authentication deadline. The May acceptance guide documents full-amount-only manual capture for Checkout, Elements and Direct API in requires_capture (old raw lines 190-205, 800-815 and 1051-1066). The separate November 7 MobilePay overview at https://docs.stripe.com/payments/mobilepay expressly permits manual and partial capture and states that a partial capture is final. Stripe releases the uncaptured remainder and a second capture cannot collect it (raw/stripe-payments-mobilepay-2026-11-07.md lines 76-80 and 90-92). Add dated reciprocal warnings in the acceptance and overview summaries, including source-stripe-mobilepay.md, and qualify the shared routes that repeat the older limit. Partial refunds are distinct (November overview lines 82-85 and 94-96). The overview establishes no effective change date or every variant's or account's support. Keep historical SDK versions and test/live examples scoped. For post-payment actions the May guide relies on payment_intent.succeeded, with PaymentIntent status used for customer messaging (old raw lines 123-153, 611-665 and 744-774). Resource creation, redirects and SDK callbacks alone do not establish payment completion.
